NHTSA lists 5 recalls for the 2020 Honda Civic. This comes from NHTSA's recalls-by-vehicle API, queried today for Honda, Civic, model year 2020.

| Campaign # | Component | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| **21V-215** | Fuel system: fuel pump | The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank may fail and stall the engine while driving. This expands recall 20V-314. |
| **23V-458** | Service brakes: master cylinder | A tie rod fastener between the brake booster and master cylinder may be improperly assembled. The master cylinder can separate from the booster and cause loss of braking. |
| **23V-858** | Fuel system: fuel pump | The in-tank fuel pump may fail and stall the engine while driving. This expands 21V-215 and 20V-314. |
| **24V-064** | Air bags: front passenger occupant-classification sensor | The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, so the air bag isn't suppressed as intended. |
| **26V-332** | Air bags: front passenger occupant-classification sensor | The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, which can cause the air bags to deploy unintentionally during a crash. It was filed 21 May 2026, so it's the newest. |

The API lists recalls by model and year. Each one applies only to certain vehicles, based on VIN and trim. Before you buy, run the specific car's VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or through Honda to see which recalls are open and which have been repaired. Recall repairs are free at a dealer. For a car with open recalls, you can ask the seller to have them done first.

I've pulled Stripe's changelog index and checked every 2025 release. Two of them carry the "Breaking changes" flag, and I'm summarizing those now.

**Caveat:** the index flags breaking changes per release, not per item. In the lists below, "Removes/Replaces/Updates…" are Stripe's own titles. I haven't opened the individual pages, so the details are only as deep as those titles. The full index is saved at `.firecrawl/changelog.md`.

## 2025-03-31.basil (first Basil release)
Billing
- Removes discount coupons that have no specified end time.
- Removes the singular `coupon` and `promotion_code` parameters, now that discounts are stackable.
- Replaces top-level price fields on Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items with a new price model.
- Replaces top-level tax properties on Invoices, Invoice Line Items and Credit Note Line Items with a new tax model.
- Adds subscription-item-level billing periods and removes the subscription-level `current_period_start` and `current_period_end`.
- Adds a `parent` field to invoicing objects that shows how each was generated.
- Replaces the Upcoming Invoice API methods with the Create Preview Invoice API.
- Removes legacy usage-based billing.

Payments and Checkout
- Removes the manual capture method for Interac cards.
- Partially capturing or canceling a payment no longer creates a Refund.
- Naver Pay payment method fields can't be modified after the object is created.
- The Vault and Forward API returns 402 for upstream request timeouts.
- Checkout Session removes shipping details.
- Checkout Sessions have lower latency and new update semantics.

Cross-product
- Removes total count expansion on list methods.
- Removes the `page` parameter.
- The Person object's political exposure property changes from a string to an enum.

## 2025-09-30.clover (first Clover release)
Billing
- Removes the `iterations` parameter on subscription schedules.
- Promotion Codes now reference Coupons through a polymorphic `promotion` field.
- Adds a Discount `source` property and removes the Discount `coupon` property.
- Flexible billing mode becomes the default for new subscriptions.
- Subscription schedule phase end dates now take billing cycle anchor changes into account.

Checkout and Elements
- Removes the currency conversion field from Checkout Sessions.
- Removes `redirectToCheckout`.
- `initCheckout` becomes synchronous.
- Default behavior changes for saved payment methods in Elements with Checkout Sessions.
- Client secrets for Intents in certain states can no longer be reused when initializing Elements.
- Removes deprecated messaging and bank Elements.
- Removes postal code for card payments in certain regions.

Payments, Issuing and Radar
- Changes the decline codes for Alma, Amazon Pay, Billie, Satispay and South Korean payment methods.
- Issuing Authorization risk levels now use standard values.
- Adds new enum values for Radar manual reviews.

## Other 2025 versions
These are all monthly releases with no breaking flag on the index: 2025-01-27 and 2025-02-24 (acacia), 2025-04-30 through 2025-08-27 (basil), and 2025-10-29, 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-15 (clover). They add features and should be backward compatible.

Stripe's changelog starts each major release (Basil, Clover) with its breaking changes, so these two are where your pin will bite. If you pin to a version earlier than 2025-03-31.basil, upgrading means going through both lists.

I built this list from a site map of vercel.com/docs and the `.md` versions of the pages. I read the title and metadata of the main pages. For the integration sub-pages and the REST API/MCP entries, I'm going by their URLs.

**Related reference pages**

- `cli/global-config`: the `vercel global-config` CLI command.

**Pages that only mention it**

- `functions/runtimes/edge` and `routing-middleware`: typical places to read from it.
- `storage`: where it sits among Vercel's data products.

NHTSA lists 5 recalls for the 2020 Honda Civic. I pulled them from the NHTSA recalls API (make=Honda, model=Civic, year=2020).

| Campaign # | Component | Problem | Reported |
|---|---|---|---|
| **21V215000** | Fuel system: fuel pump | The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank may fail. | Mar 2021 |
| **23V458000** | Service brakes: master cylinder | The tie rod fastener between the brake booster and master cylinder may have been assembled wrong, so the master cylinder can separate from the booster. | Jun 2023 |
| **23V858000** | Fuel system: fuel pump | The fuel pump inside the tank may fail. | Dec 2023 |
| **24V064000** | Air bags: front passenger occupant classification sensor | The passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, so the air bag may not be suppressed as intended. | Feb 2024 |
| **26V332000** | Air bags: front passenger occupant classification sensor | The passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, which can cause the air bags to deploy unintentionally in a crash. | May 2026 |

- **Fuel pump:** the 2021 and 2023 fuel pump recalls are separate campaigns. A car can be covered by both, and the second was a broader expansion.
- **Sensor recall:** 26V332000 is the newest, from May 2026, so many cars may not have had the remedy yet.
- **Check the specific car:** these recalls cover certain vehicles within the model year, not every 2020 Civic. Get the VIN and run it at nhtsa.gov/recalls (or Honda's lookup). That shows which recalls apply and whether the repair has been done. Recall repairs are free at Honda dealers.

I pulled Stripe's Basil, Acacia and Clover changelog pages (the main changelog was behind a captcha). I'm now writing up the 2025 breaking changes.

# Stripe breaking changes in 2025

Stripe only ships breaking changes in the first version of each release. Only two 2025 versions did that: `2025-03-31.basil` and `2025-09-30.clover`. Every other 2025 version is additive-only. That includes `2025-01-27.acacia`, `2025-02-24.acacia`, the monthly Basil versions from April to August, and the Clover versions from October to December. Acacia's breaking version, `2024-10-28.acacia`, shipped in 2024.

The version page flags the whole version as "Breaking changes". It doesn't flag individual items, and each version also bundles new features. I picked the items below from their titles and Stripe's own summaries. I didn't open the individual item pages, so check those for exact field names before upgrading.

## 2025-03-31.basil (March 31, 2025)

**Billing**
- **Subscription periods:** Subscription-level `current_period_start` and `current_period_end` are removed. Billing periods now live on each subscription item.
- **Legacy usage-based billing:** Removed.
- **Upcoming Invoice API:** Replaced by the Create Preview Invoice API.
- **Coupons:** Coupons with no specified end time are no longer supported. The singular `coupon` and `promotion_code` parameters are removed in favor of stackable discounts.
- **Invoice pricing and tax:** Top-level price fields on Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items are replaced by a new price model. Top-level tax properties on Invoices, Invoice Line Items and Credit Note Line Items are replaced by a new tax model.
- **Invoicing objects:** Invoicing resources get a new `parent` field showing how they were generated.
- **Customer balance transactions:** New transaction types are introduced.

**Checkout**
- **Subscription creation timing:** Checkout Sessions for subscriptions now create the subscription only after the customer completes payment. Stripe says this lowers latency.
- **Shipping details:** Checkout Session shipping details are removed.

**Payments**
- **Partial capture and cancellation:** Partially capturing or canceling a payment no longer creates a Refund.
- **Interac manual capture:** The manual capture method is removed for Interac cards.
- **Naver Pay:** Fields on a Naver Pay payment method can't be modified after it's created.
- **Vault and Forward API:** It now returns a 402 for upstream request timeouts.

**Other**
- **List endpoints:** You can no longer expand `total_count`.
- **Event destinations:** The `page` parameter is removed.
- **Person object:** The political exposure property changes from a string to an enum.
- **Payment Element:** The default layout is updated.
- **Issuing webhooks:** HTTP Accept headers now specify JSON for Issuing authorization webhooks.

The same version also adds several items that aren't breaking. These include the `custom` UI mode for Checkout Sessions, new meter webhooks, and new payment methods such as Billie, Satispay and NZ BECS.

## 2025-09-30.clover (September 30, 2025)

**Billing**
- **Flexible billing mode:** It is now the default for new subscriptions.
- **Schedule iterations:** The `iterations` parameter on subscription schedules is removed.
- **Promotion codes:** They now reference coupons through a polymorphic `promotion` field.
- **Discounts:** The `source` property is added and the `coupon` property is removed.
- **Phase end dates:** Subscription schedule phase end dates now account for billing cycle anchor resets.

**Checkout and Elements**
- **`redirectToCheckout`:** Removed.
- **`initCheckout`:** It is now synchronous.
- **Currency conversion:** `currency_conversion` is removed from Checkout Sessions. Use `presentment_details` instead.
- **Postal codes:** They are no longer collected for card payments in Canada, the UK and Puerto Rico.
- **Client secrets:** Elements blocks reuse of Intent client secrets in certain states.
- **Saved payment methods:** The default behavior for saved payment methods in Elements with Checkout Sessions changes.
- **Deprecated Elements:** The deprecated messaging and bank elements are removed from Stripe.js.

**Payments and other**
- **Decline codes:** The set of decline codes changes for Alma, Amazon Pay, Billie, Satispay and South Korean payment methods.
- **Issuing risk levels:** Issuing Authorization risk levels now use standard values.
- **Radar and Connect:** Radar manual review enums and Connect risk requirement descriptions are expanded. These are additive in practice, but strict enum parsing can break.

The Clover changelog also lists public-preview-only breaking changes that don't affect GA versions. These include removing platform-specific fields from v2 Accounts and restructuring the Smart Disputes `recommended_evidence` field.

## What to check if you pin a version

- **Pinned before Basil:** Subscription `current_period_*` is the change that most often breaks code. Clover also changes the default billing mode, which changes proration, trial and usage behavior.
- **Moving Basil to Clover:** Review the items under 2025-09-30.clover above.

Two caveats on completeness. The January 2026 and later Clover versions are outside your question. I also didn't confirm whether Stripe made any other breaking changes outside the versioned changelog, such as SDK major versions or Stripe.js changes.

Firecrawl's docs list ten official SDKs (nine language SDKs plus the CLI) and a separate integrations page. I read both from docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/overview and docs.firecrawl.dev/integrations.

## Official SDKs

| SDK | Install command |
|---|---|
| Python | `pip install firecrawl` |
| Node / TypeScript | `npm install firecrawl` |
| Go (needs Go 1.23+) | `go get github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/apps/go-sdk` |
| Java | Gradle (Kotlin DSL): `implementation("com.firecrawl:firecrawl-java:1.18.5")`. Gradle Groovy and Maven (`com.firecrawl:firecrawl-java:1.18.5`) are also documented. |
| Ruby (needs Ruby 3.0+) | `gem install firecrawl-sdk`, or add `gem "firecrawl-sdk", "~> 1.0"` to the Gemfile and run `bundle install` |
| Rust (needs Rust 1.70+) | `cargo add firecrawl` |
| .NET | `dotnet add package firecrawl-sdk`, or `Install-Package firecrawl-sdk` in the NuGet console |
| PHP (needs PHP 8.1+, with Laravel support) | `composer require firecrawl/firecrawl-sdk` |
| Elixir | Add `{:firecrawl, "~> 1.0"}` to the deps in `mix.exs` |
| CLI | `npm install -g firecrawl-cli`. To set up agent skills as well, run `npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest init --all --browser`. |

## Documented integrations

These are grouped as on the integrations page:

- **Coding agents and assistants:** Claude & Claude Code, ChatGPT & Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Amp, Windsurf and Antigravity. Most connect through the Firecrawl MCP server or the CLI.
- **App builders and platforms:** Replit, Lovable, Stripe Projects and Vercel Marketplace.
- **Agent frameworks:** LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, CAMEL-AI, Praison AI, Neuron AI, Vercel AI SDK and Mastra.
- **Visual AI builders:** Dify, Langflow and Flowise.
- **Workflow automation:** Zapier, Make, n8n and Pipedream.
- **Tooling and data platforms:** Composio.

I didn't open the individual integration pages. Their install steps vary: some use MCP config, some a plugin, some a package. I can pull the steps for any of them if you want.

I also saw an optional Laravel AI add-on on the PHP page. It needs `laravel/ai` and `firecrawl/firecrawl-sdk` 1.9.0 or later. The Java version (1.18.5) is what the docs showed today and may change.
